questions.why: Go through the feminine: lent → lente → lentement. That single step makes almost the whole system regular.

questions.q: What is the adverb from « heureux » ?
questions.why: The feminine is heureuse, so the adverb is heureusement. Never build -ment onto the masculine.
When the masculine already ends in a vowel, -ment attaches directly: vrai, poli, absolu, rapide all skip the feminine.
The feminine of doux is douce, giving doucement. It means gently, and also slowly.

questions.q: What is the adverb from « constant » ?
questions.why: Adjectives in -ant swap to -amment; those in -ent swap to -emment. Constant → constamment, évident → évidemment.
-ent becomes -emment. Careful with lent, which is a plain adjective, not a present participle, so it takes the ordinary route: lentement.
Bien is the adverb, describing the verb. Bon is the adjective: c'est un bon chanteur. Il chante bon is the classic error.
Mauvais is the adjective describing film; mal is the adverb describing how he acts. Same split as bon and bien.

questions.q: Build the sentence: I slept well.
questions.why: In a compound tense a short adverb sits between the auxiliary and the participle. A long one goes after it: il a répondu poliment.

questions.q: Build the sentence: I often eat here.
questions.why: In a simple tense the adverb follows the verb. French never puts it between subject and verb, however natural he often eats sounds in English.
An adverb modifying an adjective goes in front of it. Gentille is the feminine of gentil, whose own adverb is the irregular gentiment.
Couramment is fluently. Currently is actuellement — a false friend that catches almost everyone.

questions.q: Translate the opener: « ___, je suis fatigué. » (Actually, I'm tired.)
questions.why: Actuellement means currently, so actually is en fait. In the same family, éventuellement means possibly, and eventually is finalement.
An adverb commenting on the whole sentence goes at the front, marked off by a comma. Heureusement means fortunately.

questions.q: Give the three rules for forming an adverb in -ment, with an example of each, then name two ways French avoids -ment altogether.
a: 1. Default: take the feminine adjective and add -ment — lent → lente → lentement, heureux → heureuse → heureusement. 2. Masculine already ending in a vowel: add -ment directly — vrai → vraiment, absolu → absolument (a few take an accent: précis → précisément, énorme → énormément). 3. Adjectives in -ant / -ent: swap to -amment / -emment — constant → constamment, évident → évidemment. Avoiding -ment: avec + abstract noun (avec soin, en silence, avec joie), and de façon / de manière + adjective (de façon régulière).
questions.why: The three rules cover nearly every adjective; the prepositional patterns cover the rest and often sound more natural than a long -ment word.

questions.q: Build the sentence: He answered politely.
questions.why: Poliment is long, so it goes after the participle. A short adverb goes between the auxiliary and the participle.

questions.q: Build the sentence: He always drives dangerously.
questions.why: In a simple tense the adverb follows the verb, and a frequency adverb comes first when two of them meet. Dangereux is a -ant adjective, hence -amment.
